name: Apollo Lunar Module (descent)
revision: LM descent, design weights Dec 1967 (S4); engine as of Apollo 11 era

provenance.source: Ali et al., AAS-26-167 Table 2 (gear geometry from NASA CAD model); Rogers, 7th Aerospace Mechanisms Symposium 1972
provenance.units: SI (kg, N, s, Pa, m, deg)
provenance.notes: Gear geometry measured from a public CAD model and spot-checked by the authors. Vehicle origin y=0 is the footpad-bottom plane. Allowable touchdown tilt and angular rate were not found and remain blocking.

components.name: LM descent engine (LMDE/DPS)
components.description: Throttleable hypergolic descent engine, 10:1 throttle ratio.

provenance.source: NASA TN D-7143 (rated thrust, throttle, gimbal, restarts); Wikipedia Descent propulsion system (Isp, chamber pressure, mass, geometry)
provenance.units: SI (kg, N, s, Pa, m, deg)
provenance.notes: Mixed published and published-secondary values; Isp and chamber pressure at 10% and 100% only, interpolated linearly in between. Throttle 1.0 is the 10,500 lbf maximum rating; in flight the engine ran throttled to 65% or at the 92.5% fixed throttle point, with 65%-92.5% non-operating. Model chamber pressure at 10% throttle is ~83 kPa vs 76 kPa published. Duty-cycle life 1,000 s (not per-burn). Sea-level performance is unknown and likely N/A for this vacuum engine; exit area is derived from the 59 in exit diameter. Tail-off, minimum impulse and gimbal rate unknown.

provenance.source: NASA MSC IN 68-FM-78 Table II (propellant mass); Grumman LMA790-2 3-4.1 (mixture ratio 1.6)
provenance.units: SI (kg, N, s, Pa, m, deg)
provenance.notes: Loaded masses derived from total descent propellant and mixture ratio, split equally between the two tanks of each type. Tank capacity unknown: set equal to loaded mass (a lower bound). Residual/unusable propellant unknown. Tank dry mass is included in the remainder component.
